items.summary: Megaspeed says suspected China spy Alice Huang, tied to Nvidia's Jensen Huang over alleged affairs, departed its executive role in August 2025. The Singapore firm launched an internal investigation after reports it may have routed advanced AI chips to China via data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed Commerce for export oversight failures; Howard Lutnick faces Senate testimony as Nvidia remains banned from selling advanced chips to China.
items.title: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left Megaspeed; US probes chip export oversight

items.summary: Anya Schiffrin, a senior lecturer at Columbia University's School of International and Public Affairs, released a report examining how the New York City government uses online creators to disseminate public information. Her research found that influencers are sometimes paid as much as $5,000 to promote city services such as rent regulations, immigrant rights, SNAP enrollment, and pre-K registration, with activity expanding notably after the pandemic. A Signal group, which grew out of Creators for Zohran during Mamdani's campaign and is now called New York City Creators Announcements, reportedly contains more than 200 people who receive targeted bulletins about city events. The report drew intense scrutiny: within three weeks it prompted a council oversight hearing lasting three and a half hours, four pieces of draft legislation, and an ethics complaint. Schiffrin notes that the group's members are not paid but worry about precarity-driven conflicts of interest and potential misuse. She points to regulations in Spain, Italy, France, Canada, across the US, and within the EU as models for disclosure, urging New York to adopt clearer standards while acknowledging critics' concerns about double standards relative to other politicians like Hegseth.
items.title: New York City's Use of Influencers for Public Messaging and Calls for Disclosure Standards

items.summary: Singapore Airlines' announcement of next-generation aircraft interiors, involving international design firms such as PriestmanGoode, BMW Designworks and Factorydesign, prompted a question about whether capable Singapore firms could also participate alongside international specialists. Changi Airport Terminal 5 exemplifies collaboration between international architectural firms KPF and Heatherwick Studio and local firms like DP Architects, Architects 61 and Surbana Jurong. Singapore has built globally competitive companies with substantial purchasing power that can help smaller local firms grow.
items.title: Forum: Give qualified local enterprises more chances to take part in projects and create jobs

items.summary: Low Cheng Jun, a 17-year-old polytechnic student, volunteers at ServiceSG to help older residents navigate government e-services. He assists them with Central Provident Fund withdrawals, Matched Retirement Savings Scheme top-ups, Retirement Account queries and Housing Board Build-To-Order applications. Many seniors find digital forms like Singpass overwhelming, but seeing their relief when an application succeeds gives him a sense of purpose he says no classroom could provide.
items.title: Forum: Helping seniors with e-services gives me sense of purpose

items.summary: TSMC confirmed that personal data of current and former employees was leaked online after a threat actor auctioned 6.9GB allegedly stolen from the company on November 8, including national ID numbers, addresses, contact details and banking information across 46,000 employee records.
items.title: TSMC Employee Data Breach Linked to Cloud Provider

items.summary: The article argues Tesla rushed an invite-only, Texas-only Cybercab primarily to win its bet with YouTuber Marques Brownlee (MKBHD), who wagered he'd shave his head if Tesla delivered the cab for $30,000 or less before 2027. The order page lists a $29,990 price plus a mandatory $299 monthly Autonomy Subscription and a $1,000 deposit, with December 2026 delivery in geofenced Robotaxi cities only—totaling about $47,631 over five years. MKBHD called it 'a paperweight,' while Musk insisted the fee should match FSD's ~$115/month and that nationwide availability awaits regulatory approval. Critics compare it unfavorably to a Model Y with FSD for $99/month.
items.title: Tesla's Invite-Only Cybercab Looks Built to Win a Bet Against MKBHD

items.summary: Autonomous lawncare company Greenzie passed a milestone last week by surpassing 255,000 cumulative robomowing miles. The self-driving mowers have covered more than 9 billion square feet of turf across over 200 commercial customers in 45 US states and roughly 500,000 equivalent man-hours. CEO Charles Brian Quinn emphasized the commercial experience behind the achievement.
items.title: Greenzie Surpasses 255,000 Autonomous Mowing Miles

items.summary: Brazil has launched two roadmaps encouraging countries to accelerate phasing out fossil fuels and plan green transitions, offering broad frameworks for nations to develop their own national climate plans. Announced in early November ahead of COP31 in Turkey, the initiative follows President Lula da Silva's election victory over Flávio Bolsonaro. André Corrêa do Lago described them as 'documents of implementation,' urging transportation, energy, and infrastructure ministries to establish national action plans. The roadmaps recommend reducing gas flaring, cutting fossil fuel subsidies, developing renewables, supporting low-income countries against deforestation, and regulating forest-trade flows. However, Joeri Rogelj noted they lack timelines or benchmarks for the Paris Agreement's goal of limiting warming to 1.5°C.
items.title: Brazil's Fossil Fuel Roadmaps Aim to Accelerate Global Green Transition Ahead of COP31

items.summary: A rupture on the Jadranski naftovod (JANAF) pipeline on November 6 severed oil supply to Serbia's sole refinery in Pančevo, operated by US-sanctioned NIS. With no repair timeline and reports of planned production cuts, the facility relies on state reserves that may sustain operations for weeks until a December 11 sanctions-deal deadline.
items.title: Serbia's Pančevo Refinery Cut Off as JANAF Pipeline Outage Lingers Amid Sanctions Deadline

items.summary: Scout Motors has produced its first validation builds of the Traveler SUV and Terra pickup at its Blythewood, South Carolina factory, which CEO Scott Keogh says is 85% complete. The company currently holds over 200,000 reservations — with range-extended versions accounting for 87% and the Traveler capturing 75%. Actual production targets 2027, deliveries begin in 2028.
items.title: Scout Motors Advances Toward Mass Production Amid Strong Reservation Demand

items.summary: Ontario Power Generation admits its first GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 reactor at Darlington will exceed its C$7.7 billion approved budget and miss its October 2030 commercial-operation target, with no replacement cost or completion date yet. The delay stems from engineering dependencies rather than construction failures; the foundation is in place but design maturity lagged physical work. OPG withdrew its SMR generation forecast from a November filing to the Ontario Energy Board, removing planned output of about 0.5 TWh in 2030 and 1.9 TWh in 2031. The article argues each later reactor is an independent investment decision requiring outside-view cost updates before commitment.
items.title: Darlington’s First SMR Is Late and Over Budget. Ontario Needs to Rethink the Next Three.

items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that Nvidia should look beyond its ranks for a new chief executive after Jensen Huang abruptly stepped down last week amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. Bessent urged the board to bring in outside counsel and answer export-compliance questions within 10 days; the Financial Times reported the board has approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas.
items.title: Bessent Says Nvidia Must 'Go Outside' for New CEO

items.summary: Andy Burnham pledged early intervention in childhood as part of a societal rethink of youth unemployment, ahead of Alan Milburn's review. Neets topped a million this year for the first time in over a decade. The government will offer vocational training and guarantee eligible 18- to 24-year-olds a fully funded six-month job after 12 months on universal credit, with benefits as backstop rather than starting point. Milburn's report promises nearly half a million opportunities within a decade but advises sweeping changes: some lose personal independence payments or the health element of universal credit for a new youth allowance at standard rate; child mental health services receive £1bn. The bill will take 10 years to come down, with upfront investment needed. Conservatives and Reform call for immediate cuts, Kemi Badenoch vowing to slash welfare by £36.1bn by 2030.
items.title: Burnham's youth jobs plan and the benefits backstop debate

items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham argues that the crisis facing young people in the United Kingdom stems from political failure rather than individual choice. He blames the Conservative government, which he says deliberately imposed austerity on youth through Sure Start closures at age four, shut youth clubs and libraries by 12, delayed mental health support for teenagers, and devalued technical education by 18. Burnham condemns proposed welfare cuts as a path to higher spending and poverty rather than reform. He advocates investing in young people instead of punishing them, citing Alan Milburn's upcoming review as an opportunity for systemic change toward supporting childhood from the earliest years.
items.title: Andy Burnham Calls for Generational Response to Britain's Youth Crisis

items.summary: Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden backed giving government-backed employment help to young people a legislative underpinning, calling the current offer too vague. This follows former Labour minister Alan Milburn's review recommending that under-25s be guaranteed placements or training by Tuesday, though it would also cut some claimants' benefits and end access to Universal Credit's health element in England and Wales. Conservative MP Helen Whately rejected a legal guarantee as nonsensical, favouring tax cuts for employers instead. McFadden noted existing schemes like Kickstart had been temporary and less effective at reducing long-term joblessness.
items.title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

items.summary: Rockefeller International Chairman Ruchir Sharma cautioned that investors diversifying into Taiwan and South Korea may inadvertently amplify exposure to the US-led AI boom. He flagged TSMC's rising weight in emerging market equities as concerning, noting it now exceeds India's within the MSCI Emerging Markets Index.
items.title: Ruchir Sharma Warns Against Buying Taiwan and South Korea Dip

items.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is expected to travel on Air Force One with President Donald Trump to China this week as he fights to regain footing after clashing with Trump officials over Nvidia and chip controls. Republicans accuse him of slow-walking Commerce restrictions on AI chip exports, citing his close ties to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and reports involving Megaspeed. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has pushed for months to blacklist the company, but Commerce holds authority. The White House maintains confidence in Lutnick as he accompanies Trump to meet Xi Jinping at APEC.
items.title: Under Pressure, Lutnick Joins Trump in China

items.summary: Hong Kong property developer New World Development proposed on Nov 15 a rights issue to raise about HK$24.9 billion (US$3.17 billion) as it seeks to cut debt, sell assets and bolster liquidity amid tight credit and a weak market. Controlling shareholder Chow Tai Fook Enterprises owns roughly 45.3 per cent and has committed to fully underwrite the issue.
items.title: New World Development Proposes HK$24.9 Billion Rights Issue

items.summary: Former RBI Governor Raghuram Rajan questioned why India's private sector lacks global ambition, arguing that many large companies are content dominating the domestic market instead of investing in innovation and competing internationally. He noted weak private investment despite economic potential, and asked why technology giants like TCS and Infosys missed AI's initial wave.
items.title: Raghuram Rajan Questions India's Private Sector Ambition on Global Stage

items.summary: ASEAN signed its first standalone digital economy pact in Manila, aiming to ease cross-border payments and data transfers while reducing paperwork through electronic documents. The deal takes effect May 2027, replacing the 2019 e-commerce agreement. The Asian Development Bank announced up to $5 billion by 2030 to fund it. Google, Temasek and Bain forecast regional digital transactions reaching $368 billion this year.
items.title: Southeast Asia Signs Digital Economy Framework Agreement

items.summary: Monica Hardy Whaley, president of the National Center for APEC, argues that regular meetings help leaders and representatives get to know one another and build trust. Drawing on her experiences during China's three APEC host years—Shanghai in 2001, Beijing in 2014, and Shenzhen in 2026—she reflects on memorable moments and explains why sustained dialogue matters for stability and cooperation across the Asia-Pacific.
items.title: How APEC Builds Trust Through Dialogue

items.summary: This episode of a 12-episode series on the Communist Party of China examines policy continuity and the costs of arbitrary reversals. It argues that businesses, workers and families make long-term commitments—investments lasting years or decades—that cannot be reversed overnight without consequence. The Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee called for action against officials who disregard existing commitments and reverse established policies. Shanxi's Youyu County illustrates continuity: over more than 70 years, more than 20 successive county Party secretaries raised forest coverage from less than 0. 3% to more than 57%, creating a nationally renowned 'Green Oasis Beyond the Great Wall.'
items.title: Setting the Rules Straight: Policy Continuity over Arbitrary Reversals

items.summary: A Home Office plan to expand Campsfield House immigration removal centre in Oxfordshire from 160 to 400 bed spaces is facing objections. Thames Water warned detainees could face insect swarms and strong smells, with the site just 20 metres from a sewage pumping station. Campaigners say it shows disregard for human dignity, while Oxfordshire county council called for permanent closure.
items.title: Campsfield House detention expansion faces objections over sewage proximity

items.summary: Thousands gathered in central Prague on Sunday, organised by the Million Moments for Democracy association which said roughly 400,000 attended, described as the largest protest since independence in 1993. Protesters oppose scrapping the licence fee and funding Czech Television and radio from the state budget, fearing politicians could stifle media freedom. The ANO-led coalition insists editorial independence is unaffected but wants broadcasters to cut costs.
items.title: Czechs Rally Against Plan to Switch Funding of Public Media

items.summary: Marking the sixth anniversary of a symposium on advancing the Yangtze River Economic Belt, this documentary profiles the Zhoudai Bridge in east China. Built across 20-to-40-meter-thick seabed mud over harsh marine terrain with typhoons and strong currents, the 25.7-kilometer bridge links eight Zhoushan islands to the mainland as part of an 86.68-km expressway network. Engineers deployed 109-meter steel piles and BDS-GPS positioning technology for stability. More than an engineering showcase, it serves as a case study fostering coordinated regional development across the Yangtze River Delta.
items.title: Zhoudai Bridge and Mega Island-Link Connect Yangtze River Delta

items.summary: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs gathered in Prague on Sunday, with organizers Mikulas Minar estimating between 350,000 and 450,000 attendees, to protest the nationalist government's plan to replace licence-fee funding for Czech TV and Radio with state-budget payments. Critics warn this increases broadcaster dependence on the state and threatens press freedom, while the Babis-led coalition insists editorial independence remains intact.
items.title: Czechs Rally Against Public-Media Funding Overhaul

items.summary: Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia from December 1, Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna announced Sunday. The decision follows a suspected GRU arson attempt on drone maker Threod Systems in Viimsi near Tallinn; extensive damage was averted and eight Latvian residents were detained. Prime Minister Kristen Michal framed it as part of Russia's hybrid war against Europe.
items.title: Estonia Closes Russian Border After Foiled Drone Factory Sabotage

items.summary: Spain reports nearly 2,200 migrants arrived by boat at the Canary Islands this weekend. The Atlantic stretch between West Africa and the islands is one of the world's deadliest migration routes, typically traversed with ill-equipped dinghies and overcrowded boats. Over 2,000 people reached the Canaries in just 48 hours, according to a FRANCE 24 report by Sarah Morris.
items.title: Over 2,000 Migrants Reached the Canary Islands in 48 Hours

items.summary: This item is a short Euronews news bulletin dated the evening of November 15th, 2026. It promises a rapid roundup of Europe and world stories spanning business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel, framed as independent reporting with a European perspective. The piece contains no figures or named subjects to chart; it is purely an introductory framing for the bulletin's content.
items.title: Euronews Evening News Bulletin of November 15th, 2026

items.summary: Women's rights activists in Poland have opened the Abortomat, described as the world's first delivery locker supplying abortion pills. Located opposite parliament, it holds 22 pink lockers accessed via PIN codes issued by Women Help Women after a doctor-checked questionnaire. Each compartment contains mifepristone and misoprostol, taken up to the 14th week of pregnancy; because mifepristone is not registered in Poland, it must be ordered from abroad. Activists argue the machine does not break the law, though Ordo Iuris contends people behind it are committing a crime punishable by up to three years in prison. The team helps about 130 women daily at roughly €75 each. Support for right-wing parties and President Karol Nawrocki's likely veto of two recently approved bills fuel activists' concern.
items.title: Polish activists open world's first abortion-pill delivery locker amid opposition

items.summary: Tehran opened Iran's first women-only military training centre under the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' "Janfada" initiative on Tuesday, marking a notable shift since women face no mandatory conscription. Dressed in chadors, dozens of participants scaled walls and assembled rifles at Azadi Square amid IRGC officials. Sudabeh Akbari described training covering weapons, firefighting and rescue, while participant Faeze cited defending her homeland as motivation.
items.title: Iran's First Women-Only Military Training Centre Opens in Tehran

items.summary: Singapore-based Megaspeed International says Alice Huang, linked to Nvidia's Jensen Huang and suspected of routing advanced chips to China in breach of export rules, left the company last year. The firm denies wrongdoing, citing an internal investigation by outside counsel. Singapore opened its own probe into possible false server declarations; US officials have not concluded she was a spy.
items.title: Megaspeed Denies Alleged Chinese Spy Ties Amid US Scrutiny

items.summary: The WHO reported Sunday that about 3,000 people have recovered from Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo and returned home. Since May, over 11,000 confirmed cases including 5,400 deaths have been recorded across 67 health zones in eight provinces. Director-General Tedros Ghebreyesus credited local responders and global partners for progress as transmission slows, while urging safe humanitarian access, donor funding to close gaps, and community trust.
items.title: WHO Reports 3,000 Recoveries as DR Congo Battles Record Ebola Outbreak

items.summary: A deepening fuel crisis is crippling daily life across Sudan, where long queues at petrol stations have become routine amid the ongoing civil war. Drone attacks on refining infrastructure have shut down the Khartoum refinery, which once met about 70 per cent of national fuel needs, forcing reliance on imports. With gasoline now costing around $58 per gallon—up over $8 in days—and a weakening pound making imports pricier, residents face impossible choices between work and queuing for petrol.
items.title: Sudan's Fuel Crisis Paralyzes Daily Life Amid Civil War and Rising Costs

items.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 is set to become the first human-made object to travel one light-day (25.9 billion kilometers) on Nov. 18, nearly five decades after its 1977 launch. At that distance, radio signals require a minimum round-trip delay of 48 hours.
items.title: Voyager 1 Reaches One-Light-Day Distance from Earth

items.summary: The U.S. Air Force's 18th Air Wing reported that new F-15EX fighter jets arrived Sunday for permanent assignment at Kadena Air Base, Okinawa—its first overseas base to field the aircraft with advanced electronic warfare systems. The arrival begins replacing the aging F-15C/D fleet and strengthens counterair operations, deterrence, and U.S.-Japan alliance readiness.
items.title: New U.S. F-15EX Fighters Arrive at Kadena Air Base in Okinawa

items.summary: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched six drones at the Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain, the first direct strike on the Gulf state since early September's UAE attack. Iran insists a path to ending its ninth-month conflict with the U.S. remains open if Washington accepts Tehran's conditions.
items.title: Iran Strikes Bahrain Air Base as U.S. Deal Path Remains Open

items.summary: A qualitative case study of six teachers from two public secondary schools—one quintile 1 (under-resourced) and one quintile 5 (wealthiest)—in the Western Cape Metropole Central Education District examined principals' roles in supporting continuous professional teacher development. Teachers valued lifelong learning for adapting to changing learners, policy shifts, and novice teaching needs. However, no evidence showed principals directly influencing pedagogical content knowledge; indirect support occurred mainly at the quintile 5 school through senior staff arranging subject-led sessions. At the quintile 1 school, instructional leadership was seen as non-existent, with workshops viewed as tick-box exercises. The study calls on principals to identify genuine learning needs and avoid compliance-driven development.
items.title: South African Study on Principals' Role in Teacher Professional Development

items.summary: The article examines the growing role of narco brokers—financial intermediaries connecting organized crime across continents to launder illicit funds. The arrest of Bojun He, aka "El Chino," illustrates this trend; at his capture he held $2 million (quantity-108-118) and 43 million pesos (quantity-123-139). Experts Víctor Sánchez and Pablo Pérez attribute Chinese networks' appeal to intense trade that disguises illegal flows, the lowest laundering rates—3%–5% versus competitors' 10%–15% (quantity-2768-2771 through quantity-2825-2827), and methods like triangulation between China, Mexico and the U.S., informal Fei Qian transfers, crypto, ATM cash-deposit schemes, and fake invoicing. Sánchez argues laundering is harder to detect where more money circulates.
items.title: Narco Brokers and Chinese Money-Laundering Networks in Mexico

items.summary: In celebrity circles, some stars take on a key role on the big day by presiding over weddings of friends, family members and fellow performers. Their projects helped shape these lives.
items.title: Celebrities who marry celebrities: From Adam Sandler and Billie Eilish to Jimmy Kimmel, twice over

items.summary: A petition titled "Stand with Jensen" is circulating to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, reportedly gathering more than 58,000 shareholders, over 5,600 current employees, and more than 1,000 former employees. Signatures include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Boom Supersonic's Blake Scholl, and Y Combinator's Garry Tan. Petitioners argue Huang was removed without due process, that suspicion alone is insufficient grounds for ending his leadership, and demand an independent investigation with a fair hearing before any final decision. The petition emerged after Nvidia's board announced an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort following admissions of affairs, leading to his resignation; interim CEO Colette Kress was appointed while the company searches for a permanent successor.
items.title: Petition to reinstate Jensen Huang gains traction amid Nvidia leadership crisis

items.summary: Shirish Chandra Murmu, RBI Deputy Governor, speaking at an MFIN event, urged microfinance institutions to lend responsibly as borrowers face climate-related and geopolitical pressures that erode household purchasing power. He cautioned against rising loan ticket sizes fueling over-indebtedness through larger refinancing loans or overstated incomes, warned of neglecting first-time borrowers, and rejected easing the 50% loan-to-income cap despite a study showing only 18.7% of income goes to repayments.
items.title: RBI Deputy Governor Warns MFIs on Responsible Lending Amid Climate and Economic Risks

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday after being accused of three extramarital affairs, including one with businesswoman Alice Huang, who was alleged to be spying for China. Despite the fallout, some employees publicly praised him. Vartika Singh, who has worked at the company for almost eight years, lauded his humanity and leadership, recalling how he supported her family emotionally and financially while her sister battled brain cancer in California. Gavan Woolery, a senior research scientist with nearly seven years of service, said Huang personally approved his hiring during a pandemic hiring freeze and called him an exceptional leader. Separately, investors Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker urged Nvidia to consider all options for its future leadership.
items.title: Nvidia Employees Defend Jensen Huang Amid Resignation Over Affairs Scandal

items.summary: Comedian Samay Raina delivered an emotional farewell speech as he concluded Season 2 of India's Got Latent, released November 15. He revealed battling depression in Canada two years ago and turning to ChatGPT about reviving the show. Reflecting on his pre-controversy peak—every video drawing 5-6 crore views—he credited friends' support. The season featured Bollywood stars Alia Bhatt and Varun Dhawan, with rapper Raftaar as a special guest in the finale.
items.title: Samay Raina Wraps India's Got Latent Season 2 Amid Controversy Reflections

items.summary: Google announced that Google Wallet is now available as a connectable app within Gemini's Personal Intelligence settings, enabling the chatbot to analyze spending habits and assist with budgeting. Users can link their Google Wallet accounts, optionally connecting credit cards and bank accounts through Plaid for deeper insights. The feature lets users review previous-quarter spending, generate cash-flow charts, identify recurring charges, flag subscription price increases, and set seasonal budgets based on prior patterns. Security remains central: Gemini can only read account information—it cannot move or manage funds—and linking is strictly opt-in via Connected Apps under Personal Intelligence settings, disableable at any time.
items.title: Google Wallet Gains Integration for Advanced Personal Budgeting in Gemini

items.summary: A 14-year-old girl named Ruka died after falling from the sixth floor of an apartment building in Japan while livestreaming on TikTok. She was sitting on a railing when she lost her balance and fell backwards, briefly grabbing it before losing her grip. Reports say she sustained severe head injuries and later succumbed to them. As a middle school student, she had reportedly been facing personal difficulties and psychological pressures.
items.title: Japan Teen Dies Falling From Sixth Floor During TikTok Livestream

items.summary: India is betting on its semiconductor industry, which experts estimate could add over 1 lakh jobs in the next three years. The workforce, currently around 25,000 people, may expand fourfold. Specialized roles like process engineering and chip fabrication pay four to six times IT salaries. Senior talent remains scarce, prompting companies to look abroad.
items.title: Semiconductor boom may add 1 lakh jobs; senior engineers earn 6x IT salar

items.summary: Following the fallout from Jensen Huang's departure over allegations of an extramarital affair, US lawmakers across party lines are advancing bills to tighten restrictions on exporting advanced AI chips to China. The proposals would also expand Congress's authority to review and potentially block export deals already approved by the administration.
items.title: US Lawmakers Push for Tighter AI Chip Export Restrictions After Nvidia Controversy

items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh BJP rejected reports that a list of 209 candidates for the 2027 assembly elections had been prepared and sent to central leadership, calling it fabricated. State President Pankaj Chaudhary denied holding meetings on such a list, describing rumors as a 'well-planned conspiracy' meant to create fear among workers. The party said candidate selection has not begun.
items.title: BJP Refutes Reports of Pre-Prepared UP Election Candidate List

items.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat warned of efforts to divide India by exploiting smaller identities, comparing the strategy to British-era divide-and-rule policy. Speaking at an RSS Jodhpur Prant event in Shikarpura on Sunday, he said global forces opposed India becoming great and urged citizens to shed selfishness and ego. Citing the Mahabharata, Bhagwat noted that even a powerful army lost due to internal discord while unity prevailed. He emphasized grassroots leadership, calling for 25 to 100 selfless individuals in every village, street and neighbourhood dedicated to national service.
items.title: 'Divide-and-rule tactics': RSS chief Bhagwat's warning over attempts to split India

items.summary: A ₹2,000 challan issued to a motorist who allegedly drove at 101 kmph on the Yamuna Expressway (limit 100 kmph) sparked online debate. The camera logged the violation as 0°N, 0°E—mid-Atlantic Ocean—rather than an expressway location. User Anujeet Shivam (@anujitshivam) shared the screenshot and tagged Noida Traffic Police and UP Traffic Police; police directed him to e-challan helpline 7065060882.
items.title: Yamuna Expressway: Speed camera logs challan location as 0°N, 0°E; man fined ₹2,000 for driving 1 kmph above limit

items.summary: Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh performed a live concert on Sunday in Indore, where he faced attempts to prevent his visit. The 42-year-old said although many efforts were made to stop him, he kept his promise to fans and arrived without fear. Earlier emails threatening bomb blasts had been sent to the mayor's office, three banks and three private schools; police later described these messages as prima facie fake after an investigation.
items.title: Diljit Dosanjh Performs in Indore Despite Threats and Opposition

items.summary: The Gauhati High Court dismissed Hamida Begum's bail petition, describing a "very grim picture" of Assam's expulsion backlog: 1,16,946 declared foreign nationals remain unapprehended as of June 30. Justice Kalyan Rai Surana and Mridul Kumar Kalita cited an affidavit from the Assam government in their November 10 order. Begum, declared a foreigner by a Foreigners Tribunal in December 2018, exhausted legal remedies before both courts; the state contends she is now eligible for expulsion.
items.title: Gauhati HC Flags 1.16 Lakh Unexpelled Foreigners in Assam

items.summary: Ahead of next year's Punjab polls, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann used a Lok Milni event in Qadian to highlight his government's welfare record and attack rivals. He urged voters to assess parties by their actual performance rather than election-season gimmicks. Mann claimed progress in jobs—citing 71,777 merit-based positions—and canal water use rising from about 22% to roughly 85%. He criticized the Congress for internal disputes and warned that a BJP-Shiromani Akali Dal alliance could harm farmers' interests.
items.title: Punjab CM Mann urges voters to judge parties on work, not gimmicks

items.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat warned that global forces seek to prevent India from becoming great by magnifying smaller identities and provoking internal conflict, tactics he likened to Britain's divide-and-rule politics. Speaking at the RSS Jodhpur Prant's 'Maru Ninad-2026' Ghosh Shivir in Shikarpura, Bhagwat urged society to shed selfishness and ego while building an organised life rooted in Dharma.
items.title: RSS Chief Bhagwat Warns of British-Era Tactics to Divide India

items.summary: Maitreyee B Chowdhury's fourth poetry collection, I Walk Instead (Red River Press), chronicles her walks across India. The poems weave personal journeys with the subcontinent's cultural and political heritage—Nagar Sankirtan, Pandhapuri Wari, Gandhi's Dandi March—and explore themes of home, migration, gendered freedom, and belonging.
items.title: 'I Walk Instead' by Maitreyee B Chowdhury

items.summary: Hyderabad cardiothoracic surgeon Dr Lokeswara Rao Sajja, with the Sajja Heart Foundation, reported promising results from a swine study published in Scientific Reports (a Nature journal). The electrically activated mechanical valve applies a controlled negative charge to mimic blood vessels' clot-repelling endothelial glycocalyx. Three pigs received it versus three controls; all survived past 20 weeks without thrombosis after dual antiplatelet therapy stopped, while two of three controls developed clots and died. Dr Sajja cautioned the findings are preliminary.
items.title: Electrically Charged Heart Valve Shows Promise

items.summary: Police arrested a 21-year-old woman from Gurdaspur, Punjab, along with her 23-year-old male accomplice for their role in the November 3 railway track blast near 50 GB village on the Anupgarh-Suratgarh line close to the India-Pakistan border. The duo allegedly made two failed attempts before detonating a timer bomb around 9:45 pm, damaging concrete sleepers and creating a crater about two feet deep. Investigators recovered foreign-made pistols, cartridges, and ₹30,000. Preliminary findings suggest contact with Pakistan-based handlers linked to ISI who may have recruited the woman through romantic overtures. Police are now tracing financial transactions and identifying other network members.
items.title: Punjab Woman and Accomplice Arrested in Rajasthan Train Track Blast; ISI 'Romance' Recruitment Suspected

items.summary: Delhi Police arrested a man, identified as Surender, for allegedly spreading misinformation about several dead fish found floating in the Yamuna near Sonia Vihar. The arrest followed videos shared on social media two days earlier that purportedly showed the Wazirabad Water Treatment Plant amid public concern over the deaths. The cause of death remains unestablished. Surender was booked under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for causing public mischief and giving false information, then released on bail.
items.title: Delhi man arrested over fish-death misinformation in Yamuna

items.summary: IPL founder Lalit Modi announced he recently acquired British citizenship after years in the UK, posting on X with images from his September ceremony at a London town hall and thanking the Oxford Union. He described it as both privilege and responsibility, rejecting 'fugitive' labels since no criminal conviction exists, while noting his 2010 departure amid BCCI suspension.
items.title: ‘Proud to be a British citizen’: Lalit Modi announces new citizenship

items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah attacked opposition leader Rahul Gandhi for criticizing the Modi government at international forums, urging him to focus on domestic village visits instead. Speaking in Pune, Shah warned that following this path would keep Congress out of power for 30 years and accused it of damaging India's image ahead of the Bharat Summit 2026. Reviving corruption allegations against the UPA government (2004-2014), he claimed scams worth ₹12 lakh crore, while asserting no such charges exist against Modi in his 12 years in office.
items.title: Amit Shah targets Rahul Gandhi over foreign visits, warns Congress of 30 more years in Opposition

items.summary: Ratan Sheikh, a history-sheeter facing 36 criminal cases, was killed on Sunday afternoon during a police encounter in West Bengal's Birbhum district. Sheikh allegedly opened fire on officers while leading them to recover the pistol used two days earlier to injure constable Biswajit Das at Layekbazar bus stand near Bolpur. He died after being taken to Bolpur Subdivisional Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
items.title: Bengal Police Encounter Killing in Birbhum

items.summary: वायरल वीडियो जो इज़्राएल की संसद (नेतान्याहू के पतन के बाद) पर फिलिस्ठीन झंडा फहराने का दावा करता है, अस्तित्वर्थ है। गुगल लेंस और रायटर्स/टाइम्स ऑफ़ इज़्राएल सहित स्रोतों से पता चला कि घटना बरलिन में ज़ीच्टाग (बंडेस्ताग) पर हुई, जहाँ एक 22 वर्षीय ने ज़ेर्मान अनियोत फ्लैग गिराया और फिलिस्ठीन झंडा लगाया; तीन लोगों को गिरफ्तार किया गया। अक्टूबर 2026 में नेतान्याहू-लिकुड सिर्फ़ 53/120 सीटें जीतकर 61 वोटों के अधिकत तक पहुँच नहीं पाया।
items.title: फैक्ट-चेक: फिलिस्ठीन झंडा बरलिन में, न इज़्राएल की संसद पर
